extracted.intended_audience: LEAs, SEAs, Bureau of Indian Education, nonprofit organizations, institutions of higher education, Indian tribes/organizations, grant applicants and education policymakers seeking ESSA federal grants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and statutory program requirements for applying to and implementing competitive grant programs authorized under ESSA (eligibility, allowable uses, matching, evaluation, priorities, set‑asides, reporting, and grant administration). Intended to help prospective grantees design applications and comply with program rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education Innovation and Research — grant phases/purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports early-phase grants to test interventions that prior research suggests have promise; mid-phase grants for implementation and rigorous evaluation of interventions that have been successfully implemented in early phase or meet similar criteria; and expansion/replication (scale-up) of interventions found to produce a sizable impact under a mid-phase grant or similar evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the program model (similar to i3: Development, Validation, Scale-up) and the intended progression from development to rigorous evaluation to replication/expansion. Use this to align application to the appropriate phase based on prior evidence of program effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education Innovation and Research — eligible applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible applicants: LEAs; SEAs; the Bureau of Indian Education (BIE); consortia of LEAs or SEAs; nonprofit organizations; or SEAs, LEAs, or the BIE in consortia with a nonprofit, business, educational service agency, or institution of higher education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must ensure they fit one of the listed entity types or appropriate consortium configurations before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education Innovation and Research — national reservation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary may reserve up to 5 percent of program funds to provide technical assistance and disseminate best practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should expect up to 5% of appropriations may be withheld at the Secretary's discretion for TA/evaluation support rather than awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education Innovation and Research — rural set‑aside
rubrics_metrics.description: At least 25 percent of funds appropriated for the program must be used for awards to serve rural areas, contingent on receipt of enough applications of sufficient quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs serving rural areas are prioritized for at least a quarter of funding if quality applications are available; applicants serving rural communities should emphasize rural impact and quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education Innovation and Research — matching requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees must provide matching funds equal to 10 percent of their grant award (in cash or in-kind) from Federal, State, local, or private sources. The Secretary may waive this requirement on a case-by-case basis upon a showing of exceptional circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must document the source and amount of non-Federal match (10%), or include rationale/supporting documentation for a waiver request under exceptional circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education Innovation and Research — evaluation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All grantees must carry out a rigorous independent evaluation of the effectiveness of their project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should include plans and budgets for an independent, rigorous evaluation (methodology, evaluator qualifications, timeline) and demonstrate capacity to conduct/commission such evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program national reservation for building evidence (various programs)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary may reserve up to 5 percent of the appropriation for technical assistance and to evaluate the implementation and impact of program activities (noted in multiple programs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate that a small portion of program funds may be used centrally for TA and evaluation rather than direct awards; applicants should not assume full appropriation will be available for competitive awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public reporting requirement (grant programs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees are required to report publicly information about their projects, including the number and percentage of children participating and progress on performance metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should include data collection and public reporting plans, metrics to be reported, and consent/data privacy considerations for public disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promise Neighborhoods — purpose and eligible applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: support distressed communities in implementing a comprehensive continuum of coordinated services to improve outcomes birth through college in high‑poverty neighborhoods. Eligible: institutions of higher education (IHEs), Indian tribes/tribal organizations, or one or more nonprofit organizations in partnership with a high‑need LEA, IHE, local government, or Indian tribe/tribal organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should form the statutorily required partnerships and demonstrate capacity to implement comprehensive, cross‑sector neighborhood strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promise Neighborhoods — matching requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Matching: an amount equal to not less than 100 percent of the amount of the grant, from Federal, State, local, and private sources. A portion of the matching funds must come from private sources, which may include in-kind contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must document a dollar‑for‑dollar non‑Federal match and the private source portion; sustainable financing strategies strengthen applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promise Neighborhoods — priority and evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority applications: neighborhoods with schools implementing comprehensive or targeted improvement activities under Title I, Part A; and applicants that incorporate evidence‑based activities into their proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize alignment with Title I improvement efforts and use of evidence‑based strategies to increase competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promise Neighborhoods — required grantee activities and planning use
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees must include planning activities to develop pipeline services; implement those pipeline services; and continuously evaluate and improve programs based on outcome data. Grantees must use at least 50 percent of their first‑year awards, and at least 25 percent of their second‑year awards, for planning activities to develop and implement pipeline services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget narratives must allocate required proportions for planning in years one and two, and describe how planning transitions to implementation and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full‑Service Community Schools — purpose and priority conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: support planning, implementation, and operation of full‑service community schools that provide comprehensive academic, social, and health services, particularly for children in high‑poverty schools. Priority to entities serving two or more eligible schools as part of community/district strategy, consortiums with broad stakeholder representation/history of effectiveness, and those using funds for evidence‑based activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should demonstrate consortium composition, scale (2+ schools), stakeholder engagement, and evidence‑based approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set‑aside for rural areas (Full‑Service Community Schools & Promise Neighborhoods)
rubrics_metrics.description: At least 15 percent of funds awarded under Full‑Service Community Schools and Promise Neighborhoods must support projects in rural areas, assuming sufficient applications of number and quality from rural applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rural applicants are eligible for set‑aside priority; applicants should demonstrate rural need and program quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project SERV — eligibility and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Project SERV provides education‑related services (counseling, referral to mental health, etc.) to LEAs and IHEs where the learning environment has been disrupted by violent or traumatic crisis. Eligible: an LEA, IHE, or a school operated or funded by BIE in which the learning environment has been disrupted due to a violent or traumatic crisis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications for Project SERV must demonstrate the crisis‑related disruption and plan for education‑related restorative services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project SERV — extended services grant application requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For extended services grants grantees must include: (1) a demonstration of the need for funds due to a continued disruption or substantial risk of disruption to the learning environment; (2) an explanation of the proposed activities designed to restore/preserve the learning environment; and (3) a budget and budget narrative for the proposed activities. Entities that have already received an extended services grant must submit an addition to the original application meeting these requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must clearly document ongoing need, describe restorative activities, and include detailed budgets and narratives tied to proposed services.

rubrics_metrics.name: School Safety National Activities — types of assistance and example projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: support activities that improve students' safety and well‑being, promoting school safety and positive environments. Activities may be carried out through grants, contracts, cooperative agreements, or agreements with other Federal agencies. Examples: school climate transformation grants, prevention efforts, resilience promotion, and training/TA for emergency management plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals may be structured as grants, contracts, or cooperative agreements and should align with examples of previously funded projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arts in Education — eligible applicants and priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible applicants: LEAs where ≥20% students low‑income; SEAs; national nonprofit organizations; IHEs; organizations with arts expertise; museums/cultural institutions; BIE; partnerships. Priority given to national nonprofit organizations of national scope that demonstrate effectiveness or high‑quality plans for disadvantaged students or students with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National scope organizations demonstrating prior effectiveness or strong plans for disadvantaged populations should highlight national reach and evidence of impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arts in Education — allowable uses and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Uses of funds include professional development for arts educators, development/dissemination of accessible instructional materials and arts programming (including online), and national/community outreach to strengthen partnerships. Conditions: the Secretary must require entities to (1) coordinate practicable project activities with public/private cultural agencies and organizations; and (2) use assistance only to supplement, not supplant, other non‑Federal funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must describe coordination with cultural institutions and explicitly show how grant funds will supplement—rather than replace—existing non‑Federal funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arts in Education — consultation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary must consult with Federal agencies/institutions, arts educators (including professional associations), and organizations representing the arts (including State/local arts agencies involved in arts education).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should demonstrate awareness of or incorporation of Federal/state arts education guidance and collaboration with relevant arts organizations where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ready to Learn — eligible applicants and capacity requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Only public telecommunications entities are eligible. Applicants must have capacity to develop/distribute high‑quality educational/instructional TV programming accessible to disadvantaged preschool/elementary children; contract with producers; negotiate contracts to return appropriate share of income from product sales; and target programming/materials to meet state/local needs while providing local outreach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must document production/distribution capacity, contracting experience, revenue‑sharing practices, and strategies for targeting and outreach to disadvantaged children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ready to Learn — consultation/coordination and use of funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees are required to consult with ED and HHS on maximizing use of quality educational programming and coordinate with other Federal early childhood training programs. At least 60 percent of funding must be used to develop educational TV programming and accompanying support materials/services, nationwide distribution‑ready programming and digital content, and contracts to ensure wide distribution; remaining funds may support education/training materials and interactive programs promoting school readiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget must allocate minimum 60% to core programming and distribution activities; describe consultations with ED/HHS and coordination with federal programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Javits Gifted and Talented Education — purpose and eligible uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: support research, demonstration projects, innovative strategies, and other activities to build capacity to identify gifted/talented students and meet their needs. Use of funds: research on identification/teaching methods, applying methods to all students (including low‑income/at‑risk), establishing/operating programs including innovative methods to reach traditionally underserved students, and providing technical assistance and dissemination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should focus on research/demonstration or capacity building, and highlight plans to serve underserved gifted populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indian Education — eligible applicants and allowable demonstration grant areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible: SEAs, LEAs, Indian Tribes/organizations, federally supported schools for Indian students, Indian IHEs, or consortia. The statute authorizes demonstration grants in areas including innovative educational programs, remedial instruction, bilingual/bicultural programs, health/nutrition services, graduation rate improvement, guidance/counseling, early childhood, LEA‑IHE partnerships, school‑to‑work, family literacy, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must be from eligible tribal/education entities and should clearly link proposed activities to the listed permissible demonstration areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indian Education — Professional Development grant requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible applicants: IHEs or SEAs/LEAs/Indian Tribes/organizations and BIE‑funded schools in consortium with IHEs. Purpose: increase number of Indian individuals qualified in teaching/school administration and improve skills. Individuals receiving training are required to secure employment in a field related to their education and benefiting Indians, or to repay assistance. Awards focus on pre‑service teacher and administrator training. Duration: 5 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs must include commitments/agreements for trainees to serve in relevant positions or repayment terms; consortia arrangements should be documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indian Education — National Activities purposes and new authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports research/evaluation/data collection on educational status of Indians; grants to support native language immersion schools/programs; grants to Tribes for administrative planning/development/coordination. ESSA established two new authorities: (1) TEA capacity building for administering education programs and promoting collaboration with SEAs; (2) Native language immersion grant program for school‑based instruction in Native languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should align with research/data needs, language preservation, Tribal administration capacity, and may target newly authorized activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Native Hawaiian Education — eligibility, priorities, and uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible applicants: Native Hawaiian educational organizations and community‑based organizations, public/private nonprofits, agencies, and institutions with experience in Native Hawaiian programs or instruction in the Native Hawaiian language. Secretary must give priority to projects addressing beginning reading/literacy in K–3, at‑risk children/youth, needs in underemployed fields, and use of Hawaiian language in instruction. Uses include early childhood, family‑based centers, literacy (Hawaiian or English), services for students with disabilities, gifted/talented instruction, curricula and vocational programs, PD, community learning centers, postsecondary access, and research/data collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should emphasize K–3 literacy, at‑risk youth supports, workforce/underemployment fields, and Hawaiian language components where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alaska Native Education — eligibility and required/permissible activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible applicants: Alaska Native organizations/entities with charter from Alaska Native tribe/org or in partnership with SEA/LEA. Mandatory activities: develop/implement plans, methods, strategies, activities to improve Alaska Native educational outcomes and collect data to evaluate programs. Permissible activities: culturally informed curricula/materials to preserve Native languages, PD, early childhood/parenting programs, student enrichment including STEM, graduation rate improvement programs, parent involvement strategies, and career preparation activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must include the mandatory plan and data collection components; permissible activities should be tied to culturally informed strategies and measurable outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preschool Development Grants — planning/renewal eligibility and matching
rubrics_metrics.description: Planning Grants: support statewide needs assessments, strategic planning, family awareness/involvement, sharing best practices, and improving program quality. Eligibility: States. Duration: not more than 1 year and may be renewed. Matching: each State must provide non‑Federal funds (cash or in‑kind) equal to not less than 30 percent of the grant for planning and renewal grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must include 30% non‑Federal match and document planning activities and partnerships across mixed delivery systems. Priority to States that have never received prior planning/development grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preschool Development Grants — renewal grants and subgrant limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Renewal Grants: to improve program quality and expand access through subgrants in a mixed delivery system; duration not more than 3 years with no renewal. Subgrant awards: in first year States may use not more than 60 percent of grant funds for subgrants; in second and third years not more than 75 percent may be used for subgrants. States must prioritize activities to improve identified needs in rural areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State applications must plan subgranting proportions by year and prioritize rural needs and quality improvement activities; demonstrate capacity to administer subgrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding Transferability — eligible programs and constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: SEAs and LEAs may transfer funds received by formula under certain programs to other specified programs to address State/local needs. The law removed limits on the amount transferable and changed which programs may transfer to/from which others. Funds can only be transferred to (never from): Title I, Parts A/C/D; Title III, Part A; Title V, Part B. Funds can be transferred to and from: Title II, Part A; Title IV, Part A; Title IV, Part B (21st CCLC). An SEA/LEA may not transfer funds it receives under any other ESEA program not listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LEAs/SEAs must check the statute's lists to determine allowable transfers; transfers are permitted among listed programs but not from the protected programs; procedural requirements may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local Flexibility Demonstration Agreements — eligibility and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary may enter into local flexibility demonstration agreements with up to 50 LEAs. Agreements are for not more than 3 years, but may be renewed for additional 3‑year terms if the LEA met requirements and is likely to continue to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LEAs seeking demonstration status must meet application requirements and ongoing performance conditions to renew.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local Flexibility — application assurances
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must provide: a description of the school funding system based on weighted per‑pupil allocations; a list of funding sources the LEA will include; the amount and percentage of total LEA funding allocated through the system; and per‑pupil expenditures of State/local funds and eligible Federal funds for the preceding fiscal year for each school served by the LEA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must include comprehensive financial transparency and documentation of current per‑pupil funding to support the proposed weighted funding model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements of the LEA's school funding system (equitable per‑pupil funding)
rubrics_metrics.description: The school funding system must: allocate a significant portion of funds (State/local and eligible Federal) to the school level based on number of students and a LEA‑developed weighted per‑pupil formula; allocate substantially more funding using weights/amounts to English learners, low‑income students, and other characteristics chosen by the LEA; ensure each high‑poverty school receives in the first year more per‑pupil funding for low‑income students than the prior year and at least as much per‑pupil funding for English learners as the prior year; be used to allocate a significant percentage of all the LEA's State/local and eligible Federal funds; include all school‑level actual expenditures (personnel and non‑personnel) in the calculation; demonstrate annually that no high‑poverty school received less per‑pupil funding for low‑income students or English learners compared to the prior year; and make public detailed per‑pupil expenditures for each school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LEAs must design weighted allocation formulas, include comprehensive expenditure calculations, publish per‑school expenditure details, and demonstrate year‑over‑year maintenance/increase of funding for targeted groups. Consult stakeholders during development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local Flexibility — consultation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The LEA must develop and implement the local flexibility demonstration agreement in consultation with teachers, principals, other school leaders (including charter leaders where applicable), administrators of Federal programs impacted by the agreement, parents, community leaders, and other relevant stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should document stakeholder engagement and processes used to develop the funding system and assurances.
